problem:
Consider the matrix $T$ and the vector $v$ given below. If $T$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T,$ find $T(v).$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

activity_context.topic_title: The Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation

feedback.problem:
Consider the matrix $T$ and the vector $v$ given below. 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ -1 & 5 & 2 \\ 6 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

If $T$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T,$ find $T(v).$

| $T(v)=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-2}} |  |  |
|  | {{field-3}} |  |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the fact that $\,T(v)=T\cdot v,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =T\cdot v \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ -1 & 5 & 2 \\ 6 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}19 \\ -5 \\ 15\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
